**Gross margin fell 0.46 points from Q1 to Q2, even though gross profit rose in dollars.**

| | Q1 (Jan–Mar) | Q2 (Apr–Jun) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales | $6,021,218 ([IS_2026-03.xlsx]Total!C13) | $6,748,503 ([IS_2026-06.xlsx]Total!C13) | |
| Gross profit | $1,691,928 ([IS_2026-03.xlsx]Total!C20) | $1,865,328 ([IS_2026-06.xlsx]Total!C20) | +$173,400 (+10.2%) ([IS_2026-03.xlsx]Total!C20, [IS_2026-06.xlsx]Total!C20) |
| Gross margin % | 28.1% ([IS_2026-03.xlsx]Total!C21) | 27.6% ([IS_2026-06.xlsx]Total!C21) | -0.46 pts ([IS_2026-03.xlsx]Total!C21, [IS_2026-06.xlsx]Total!C21) |

**What moved the rate**

The margin bridge splits the change into two effects:
- **Mix effect: -0.83 pts.** Wholesale is the lowest-margin unit, and its share of net sales rose from 65.0% to 69.7%. Online fell from 27.5% to 23.7% and Service from 7.5% to 6.5%. Both of those units have higher margins.
- **Rate effect: +0.37 pts.** Each unit's own margin improved slightly:
  - Wholesale: 21.93% to 22.31%
  - Online: 37.86% to 38.22%
  - Service: 45.84% to 46.09%

The shift toward Wholesale outweighed the small margin gains inside each unit, so the company rate fell.

**On the cause:** the statements show amounts, not reasons, so they don't explain why the mix shifted. The Q2 report has one comment from the Controller (July 8, 2026): "Wholesale: deliveries under the Harbor County schools supply agreement began in April." ([IS_2026-06.xlsx]Total!A36). That comment is the author's note. It doesn't say the agreement caused the mix shift, and I can't confirm that from the data.
